items.title: Enlarging two bounded subcomplexes to a common pair that kills a derived-tensor kernel and catches an image, inside a cardinal bound
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma concerns an arbitrary ring map A -> B, complexes M of A-modules and N of B-modules, a map a : M -> N that becomes an isomorphism after the derived tensor product with B, and given subcomplexes M_1, N_1 compatible under a; the conclusion produces enlarged subcomplexes M_2, N_2 with an explicit cardinal bound max(kappa, |M_1 union N_1|) that kills one kernel and catches one image in every cohomological degree (statement lines 29894-29921). The proof is not a routine diagram chase: it first has to build a filtered system of small subcomplexes generated by finitely many elements, with a size estimate, then estimate the cohomology of the derived tensor product through a free resolution of B of cardinality at most kappa, and finally use that the derived tensor product commutes with the filtered colimit to realize each individual obstruction in a single small stage (proof lines 29935-29988). The closing step is a cardinality count over the index set of the two sums that define M_2 and N_2, so the bound in property (3) is genuinely proved rather than assumed (proof lines 29990-30009). Every input is inside the counted span except the standard facts about cardinals, free resolutions and filtered colimits that are named in the editorial notes; the author marks two sub-steps as having details omitted, both of which are routine and none of which is load-bearing for the main line.
